## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle *zhòuběn* 呪本 — a "spell-only" extract giving the *Mahā-karuṇā-dhāraṇī* in pure transliteration without its narrative frame. Translated by **Vajrabodhi** ([金剛智](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%89%9B%E6%99%BA), 671–741), the South-Indian master and teacher of Amoghavajra, who introduced the *Vajra-śekhara* cycle into Tang Buddhism. The spell-text is parallel to the dhāraṇī embedded in [KR6j0260](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0260) (Bhagavaddharma's full sūtra) but reflects a slightly different Sanskrit *Vorlage* and a more rigorous Esoteric Indic phonology.

**Abstract**

The *zhòuběn* gives the **Mahā-karuṇā-dhāraṇī** alone — the eighty-four-*pada* spell — preceded only by the standard refuge ("namo ratna-trayāya, namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya …") and followed by no further narrative or ritual matter. The work was produced as a practical recitation aid for cultivators of the **Vajra-śekhara** cycle: rather than a full sūtra, it furnishes the spell formula cleanly transcribed for liturgical use. Its principal scholarly value is as an independent eighth-century witness to the *Nīlakaṇṭhaka-dhāraṇī* in Tang transcription, supplementing the seventh-century rendering by Bhagavaddharma in [KR6j0260](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0260) and informing subsequent Tángmì *Sahasrabhuja* manuals ([KR6j0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0269), [KR6j0272](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0272), [KR6j0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0273)). The transliteration shows that Vajrabodhi was working from a reasonably classical Sanskrit recension rather than a Prakritised one, and his spelling-conventions correspond to the standard Tángmì scribal apparatus of the *Vajra-śekhara* school.
